message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Compute Engine instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU (or the closest supported GPU if the A6000 isn’t available) running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example is provided in two ways:

| Method | What you’ll run |
|--------|-----------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | One‑liner that you paste into a terminal |
| **REST API** | JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine endpoint (use `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client) |

> ⚠️ **Important** – Google Cloud does **not** offer an “EC2” product; the equivalent is **Compute Engine**.  
> The RTX A6000 is *not* currently listed among the GPUs that Google Cloud supports. The closest match is the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** (or the older **V100** if you need a legacy GPU).  
> If you absolutely need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to use a different provider (e.g., AWS, Azure, or a local GPU host).  
> The examples below assume you’re okay with the A100; just replace the accelerator type if you find a newer GPU that Google Cloud supports.

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# Replace the placeholders with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
    --accelerator="count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a100" \   # <-- change to A6000 if available
    --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: your init script
    --tags="http-server,https-server" \
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS boot image |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one GPU of the specified type |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Terminate the VM during maintenance (GPU‑friendly) |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs at boot |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules |
| `--scopes` | IAM scopes for the VM (full cloud‑platform access) |

> **Tip:** If you need a custom machine type (e.g., 16 vCPUs, 64 GB RAM), replace `n1-standard-8` with `custom-16-65536`.

---

## 2. REST API (JSON)

Below is the JSON body you would POST to the Compute Engine API.  
Use `curl` or any HTTP client; remember to supply an OAuth 2.0 bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`).

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential\n"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### POST request example (curl)

```bash
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> Replace `@instance.json` with the path to a file containing the JSON above.

---

## 3. Things to Check Before Running

| Item | Why it matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Billing enabled** | GPU instances incur extra charges. |
| **GPU quota** | Verify you have a GPU quota for the region. |
| **API enabled** | Enable the Compute Engine API in the Cloud Console. |
| **GPU license** | Some GPUs require a license; the Compute Engine API handles this automatically. |
| **Firewall rules** | Ensure you allow SSH (port 22) and any other ports you need. |
| **Region availability** | GPUs are only available in certain zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`). |

---

## 4. Quick FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Can I use an RTX A6000?** | Google Cloud currently does not list the RTX A6000. Use the A100 or V100 instead. |
| **What if I need more GPUs?** | Add `"acceleratorCount": 2` (or more) and adjust the machine type accordingly. |
| **Do I need a startup script?** | Optional, but useful for installing drivers, CUDA, or your own software. |
| **How do I attach a persistent SSD?** | Add another entry in the `disks` array with `"boot": false`. |
| **Can I use a custom image?** | Replace the `sourceImage` field with your own image link. |

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=my-gcp-project \
    --zone=us-central1-a \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a100 \
    --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure
```

Replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with the GPU type you actually want (if Google Cloud offers it).  
That’s all you need to spin up a GPU‑enabled Ubuntu 20.04 instance on Google Cloud!
